candidates.package: SMD,6x6mm (H=4.7mm max, confirmed via CENKER datasheet)
candidates.fit: INDUCTOR 2.2uH/~1MHz option: Isat 6.75A, DCR 14mOhm, best margin-to-price of any candidate in this sweep; height 4.7mm confirmed (6x6mm footprint, smaller than the 4.7uH picks).
INDUCTOR 2.2uH/~1MHz: identical spec to CKCS6045-2.2uH (Isat 6.75A/DCR 14mOhm), second-source for #1.

REVERSE-POLARITY PMOS, top pick: Vds -30V, Id 62A (huge headroom), Rds(on) 8mOhm@10V AND 11.5mOhm@4.5V (both given) - meets <=30mOhm@10V and the <=100mW-at-2.4A target even at the low-line gate corner. Cheapest, deepest stock of any qualifying part.

REVERSE-POLARITY PMOS, compact alt: Vds -30V, Id 14A, Rds(on) 9.5mOhm@10V AND 14.7mOhm@4.5V (both given) - conduction loss at 2.4A/14.7mOhm = ~85mW, meets the 100mW target with margin in a much smaller SO-8 footprint than the DPAK picks. Note: brand on this LCSC row is a UMW rebrand, not the original Alpha&Omega AO4407A; electrically equivalent per the parametric data.
REVERSE-POLARITY PMOS alt: Vds -30V, Id 85A, Rds(on) 8mOhm@4.5V (best-in-class at the low-line gate corner) but no @10V figure given on this LCSC row; pricier than AOD403.
REVERSE-POLARITY PMOS alt: Vds -30V, Id 75A, Rds(on) 15mOhm@4.5V (no @10V figure on this row); third DPAK second-source, most expensive of the three.

REVERSE-POLARITY PMOS, well-known jelly-bean alt: Vds -30V, Id 11.4A, Rds(on) 35mOhm@4.5V - only Rds figure on this row misses the <=100mW-at-2.4A target (~201mW) but is a very common, easy-second-source SO-8 part if the architect wants industry-standard name recognition over the tightest loss number.
INPUT FUSE, top pick: one-shot 4A/63V SMD fuse, Melting I2t=1.73 A^2s (fast-acting class), deepest stock of any non-resettable candidate found.
INPUT FUSE alt: one-shot 4A/32V (right at the >=32V floor), Melting I2t=2.5356 A^2s (slower than #1) - use if 63V rating is unnecessary overkill and a slower blow curve is preferred.
INPUT FUSE alt: one-shot 4A/63V, Melting I2t=4.145 A^2s (slowest/most surge-tolerant of the shortlist), cheapest unit price.
INPUT FUSE alt: Littelfuse-branded (recognized fuse maker, easier to defend in a safety review), one-shot 4A/32V, I2t=1.764 A^2s.
INPUT FUSE alt: one-shot 4A/72V, no I2t published on this row; very deep stock, similar price to #1.

INPUT TVS, top pick: unidirectional, Vrwm 20V (>= the 20V floor, will not conduct at the 18V max input), Vc 32.4V (slightly above the ~30V aim but this is the standard part in this class - going to the next size up (22A) raises Vc to 35.5V instead), Ipp 18.6A. Deepest stock/cheapest of the class.
INPUT TVS alt: identical spec to #1 (Vrwm 20V/Vc 32.4V/Ipp 18.6A), Shandong Jingdao brand, cheapest unit price in the sweep.

INPUT TVS, smaller-footprint alt: same Vrwm 20V/Vc 32.4V as the SMB parts but lower Ipp (12.3A) in the smaller SMA package - fine for hot-plug/ESD-class transients, less margin for a sustained fault than SMB.
INPUT TVS, more-standoff-margin alt: Vrwm 22V (more margin above the 18V max input) but Vc rises to 35.5V (further from the ~30V clamp aim) - a standoff-vs-clamp tradeoff for the architect to weigh.

INPUT TVS, small-package/branded alt: Nexperia, Vrwm 20V/Vc 32.4V matching SMBJ20A electrically but in the smallest allowed package class (SOD-123W); much pricier and lower stock than the SMB/SMA parts.

Vendor drawing shows body depth 10.0mm, height ~14.1mm above the PCB - RISK: that is within ~1mm of the board's 15mm max component-height cap (A8), leaves almost no margin. candidates.package: THT plugin, 5.08mm pitch, 2P; body ~10.7mm deep x 14.1mm tall (confirmed from Kefa vendor drawing)
candidates.fit: SCREW TERMINAL alt: confirmed via vendor drawing at UL 10A/300V (IEC 24A/250-630V depending on class), meets the floor on the UL figure. Body height 14.10mm - same tight-against-15mm-cap risk as #1.
SCREW TERMINAL, cheapest alt: 15A/300V parametric rating, through-hole; height not independently confirmed for this specific closed-box variant - check against the 15mm cap before committing.

SCREW TERMINAL alt: 16A/300V parametric rating (M2 screw, smaller screwhead than the M2.5 parts above), DORABO brand, similar depth/height class to #1/#2 by family resemblance - confirm height independently.

CERAMIC (input side), top pick: 10uF/25V/X5R/0805, JLC BASIC part with 10.4M stock - meets the >=25V input floor (X5R is explicitly allowed) at Basic-tier cost/simplicity. DC-bias derating caveat: a 10uF/0805/25V X5R part will lose a large fraction (commonly 40-60%) of its rated capacitance at the ~12-18V input bias; size the effective/derated value, not the nameplate 10uF, when doing the input-ripple calc.

CERAMIC (input side) alt: 10uF/25V/X7R/1206 - X7R holds capacitance better under DC bias than the X5R Basic pick and has a wider temp range, at Extended-tier cost; same DC-bias-derating caveat applies (less severe than X5R but still significant at 25V-rated/1206).

CERAMIC (output side), top pick: 22uF/16V/X7R/1206 - well above the >=10V output floor for margin, which also reduces DC-bias derating at the 5V rail bias point vs a tighter 10V-rated part. Same caveat: check derated capacitance at 5V bias, not nameplate 22uF.

INPUT BULK CAP, top pick: SMD aluminum-polymer, 47uF/35V (well above the 25V floor for margin), ripple current 2.1A@100kHz - this is the switch-mode-suited, high-ripple/low-ESR class the requirement asks for (plain general-purpose SMD electrolytics found in the same sweep only rate 35-230mA@120Hz ripple, unsuited to a 500kHz-1.2MHz buck's input ripple duty).
INPUT BULK CAP alt: SMD aluminum-polymer, 47uF/25V (at the floor, less margin than #1), ESR 30mOhm, ripple current 2.8A@100kHz (best ripple figure of the SMD polymer options found); pricier than #1.
